controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudtrail` events with `errorCode="AccessDenied" OR errorCode="UnauthorizedAccess" OR errorCode="Client.UnauthorizedAccess"` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.1 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudtrail` traffic without `errorCode="AccessDenied" OR errorCode="UnauthorizedAccess" OR errorCode="Client.UnauthorizedAccess"`. Confirm UC-4.1.1 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" errorCode="AccessDenied" OR errorCode="UnauthorizedAccess" OR errorCode="Client.UnauthorizedAccess"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.1_unauthorized_api_calls_1"
| sort -_time
description: AccessDenied errors reveal reconnaissance activity, compromised credentials with insufficient permissions, or misconfigurations. Early indicator of attack or drift.
value: On AWS, 'Unauthorized API Calls' provides an operational signal for cloud security and governance when baseline thresholds are tuned to your account/subscription footprint. UC-4.1.1 drives high-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Configure CloudTrail to send logs to an S3 bucket. Set up the Splunk_TA_aws with an SQS-based S3 input for CloudTrail. Alert when a single principal gets >5 access denied errors in 10 minutes.
visualization: Table (principal, API call, source IP, count), Bar chart by principal, Map (source IP GeoIP).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Change.All_Changes
  where (match(All_Changes.status, "(?i)AccessDenied|UnauthorizedAccess|Client\\.UnauthorizedAccess")
     OR All_Changes.action="failure" OR match(All_Changes.command, "(?i)accessdenied|unauthorized"))
  by All_Changes.user All_Changes.src All_Changes.command span=10m
| where count > 5
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Change (All_Changes): requires CloudTrail API outcomes mapped to Change fields via Splunk_TA_aws/CIM. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Pentest or vulnerability scanning that intentionally hits forbidden APIs; new least-privilege rollouts; automation that lost IAM scope after a change window.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure CloudTrail to send logs to an S3 bucket. Set up the Splunk_TA_aws with an SQS-based S3 input for CloudTrail. Alert when a single principal gets >5 access denied errors in 10 minutes.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" errorCode="AccessDenied" OR errorCode="UnauthorizedAccess" OR errorCode="Client.UnauthorizedAccess"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.1_unauthorized_api_calls_1"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect unauthorized api calls. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_1_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (principal, API call, source IP, count), Bar chart by principal, Map (source IP GeoIP)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of unauthorized api calls so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
